Implication does not remove the linear directions. Every attribute is read out exactly, by an affine map, from the full-rank spectral embedding, and the recovered incidence and its concept lattice equal the generating ones. What implication changes is the spectrum. On a balanced b-ary tree, the eigenvectors are branch contrasts rather than one per attribute. A branching at depth ℓ gives eigenvalue μ_ℓ = w Σ_{ℓ′>ℓ} λ_ℓ′ b^(D−ℓ′), with multiplicity (b−1)bˡ, and these fall strictly with depth for any positive strengths. So a rank-(b^K − 1) embedding reads out exactly the attributes of depth at most K. Below the cut, each attribute's readout is the same constant on every descendant of its depth-K ancestor, so siblings merge. Along a tree, PMI additivity is therefore the same thing as piecewise constancy on the finest groups: it has content only where attributes cross-cut, as in analogy families.
